title: Love, Knowing, Faith, and Belief
notes: This chunk is dense, law-positive, and structurally clean: the four-office table, the love/hate axis, and the knowing-as-marriage argument land with force and almost no hedging. Scripture is woven tightly into the claims rather than parked beside them. Residual defects are mostly house-style: two author-prose sentences open with And/But, one explicit director cue (“Mark where”), two soft “Read…” imperatives that stage the reader, and a single inconsistent book abbreviation (Num). Fix those surgically and the voice stays intact.

This chunk assembles sheep/voice/name with the four terms into one visible obedience, using dense scriptural chaining and the emunah picture of steady hands. The law-positive case that works equal commandment-keeping is assertive and clear. Residual defects are house-style And openings in author prose, plus presenter cues that break the assert-only register. One relative clause is slightly tangled. No quote, doctrine, or factual mismatches appear; the modern bias analogy is left as deliberate authorial choice.

proposals.old: And John's second epistle runs the whole chain in three verses, and swears none of it is new:
proposals.new: John's second epistle runs the whole chain in three verses, and swears none of it is new:
proposals.summary: Remove banned And-opening in author prose.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author sentences starting with And. Dropping the conjunction keeps the claim and the following quote intact.

proposals.old: Read it so, and the audit is exact: gifts without obedience are a cymbal — sound with nothing inside.
proposals.new: Defined so, the audit is exact: gifts without obedience are a cymbal — sound with nothing inside.
proposals.summary: Replace reader-directive “Read it so” with assertive phrasing.
proposals.rationale: “Read it so” is a soft director cue. “Defined so” keeps the logical hinge to 1 John 5:3 without staging the reader.

proposals.old: Mark where the hymn lands: __“I shall *know* just as I also am *known*”__ — Paul's love chapter ends in the covenant word this chapter defines next.
proposals.new: The hymn lands on the covenant word this chapter defines next: __“I shall *know* just as I also am *known*”__.
proposals.rationale: “Mark where” is an explicit house-style director cue. The rewrite asserts the landing point and preserves the knowing link without the stage direction.

proposals.old: with whom God spoke __“face to face, even plainly, and not in *riddles*”__ (Num 12:8).
proposals.new: with whom God spoke __“face to face, even plainly, and not in *riddles*”__ (Numbers 12:8).
proposals.summary: Expand inconsistent book abbreviation to full name.
proposals.rationale: Every other citation in the chunk uses the full book name. “Num” is the only abbreviation and breaks internal consistency.

proposals.old: But Jesus turns away people whose facts are exactly right:
proposals.new: Jesus turns away people whose facts are exactly right:
proposals.summary: Remove banned But-opening in author prose.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author sentences starting with But. The contrast is already clear from the preceding sentence.

proposals.old: Read __“iniquity”__ in the New Testament and this is usually the word underneath — law-breaking, wearing a vaguer name.
proposals.new: In the New Testament __“iniquity”__ is usually this word underneath — law-breaking, wearing a vaguer name.
proposals.rationale: The imperative stages the reader. The rewrite states the lexical fact directly and keeps the link to anomia from the prior sentence.

proposals.old: And they follow no other — __“a sym:sym-stranger[stranger] will they not follow… for they know not the sym:sym-voice[voice] of strangers”__ (John 10:5): the stranger is the one outside the covenant, so His sheep will not heed the voice, the teaching, of those outside it. __“He calleth his own sym:sym-sheep[sheep] by sym:sym-name[name]”__ (John 10:3) — and the sym:sym-name[name] is a symbol with its own chapter just ahead.
proposals.new: They follow no other — __“a sym:sym-stranger[stranger] will they not follow… for they know not the sym:sym-voice[voice] of strangers”__ (John 10:5): the stranger is the one outside the covenant, so His sheep will not heed the voice, the teaching, of those outside it. __“He calleth his own sym:sym-sheep[sheep] by sym:sym-name[name]”__ (John 10:3) — and the sym:sym-name[name] is a symbol with its own chapter just ahead.
proposals.summary: Remove banned And sentence open in author prose.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author sentences starting with And. Dropping it preserves the claim and flow without loss.

proposals.old: Now read that famous verse whole:
proposals.new: The famous verse states it whole:
proposals.summary: Replace director cue with assertive lead-in.
proposals.rationale: “Now read” is presenter staging banned by house style. The replacement keeps the structural role and density.

proposals.old: And Abraham, who __“believed in the LORD”__ (Genesis 15:6), is shown to have been __“justified by works, when he had offered Isaac”__ (James 2:21) — the believing and the obeying are one act.
proposals.new: Abraham, who __“believed in the LORD”__ (Genesis 15:6), is shown to have been __“justified by works, when he had offered Isaac”__ (James 2:21) — the believing and the obeying are one act.
proposals.summary: Remove banned And sentence open in author prose.
proposals.rationale: House style forbids author sentences starting with And. The claim and scripture links remain identical.

proposals.old: So the sentence James wrote completes itself: faith without works is dead because the works are the commandments done — the keeping this chapter has been proving — and a faith that keeps nothing holds nothing.
proposals.new: So the sentence James wrote completes itself: faith without works is dead because the works are the commandments done — the keeping that this chapter has been proving — and a faith that keeps nothing holds nothing.
proposals.summary: Insert missing relative that for smoother clause.
proposals.rationale: The reduced relative is slightly tangled and slows the claim. Adding “that” clarifies without changing meaning or density.

proposals.old: See, then, what the symbols do to the simplest promise of all.
proposals.new: The symbols do this to the simplest promise of all.
proposals.summary: Replace imperative staging with direct assertion.
proposals.rationale: “See, then” functions as a director cue. The rewrite keeps the pivot role and author voice.

proposals.old: Then remember the many this chapter has already met — who prophesied and did wonders *in that name*, and were not known.
proposals.new: The many this chapter has already met — who prophesied and did wonders *in that name*, and were not known.
proposals.rationale: The phrase stages the reader rather than asserting. Removing it leaves the contrast intact and denser.
